turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why did you ask for this meeting?
Thanks for coming in. I should have called before the zero went in. That was wrong.
Okay. Who decided on the zero, and what was it based on?
Were you home the night of October 28?
I'm not the one being questioned. Who decided on the zero, and what was it based on?
I'm asking because it matters. Were you home?
Not answering that. You entered a zero, so what was it based on?
Did you see Owen working on the essay that night?
I'm his lawyer in this room, not your witness. Your own procedure says you speak to the student first and software alone proves nothing. What else do you have?
You're not answering. Why not?
Because you're asking me to build your case for you. You called this meeting, so show me a document.
Is there something about that night you don't want to tell me?
No. Is that your evidence, a feeling about a night? Show me something dated, or we're done here.
If he wrote it, you'd just say so. Did you see him write it?
That's a leading question, and my answer to it is the same as before. You have a zero in the gradebook, so put a document on the table.
I'll ask one more time. What did you see that night?
I'm not a witness, Hale, and asking a fifth time doesn't change that. Either you have something I can check, or I'm walking to the principal's office.
Okay. Then let me show you the version history. Created 11:31 PM, title only. 612 words at 11:52, 794 at 11:58, then 23 minutes of formatting.
Say that again slowly. Okay, I'm writing those times down. He could have drafted somewhere else and pasted it in, so what shows he didn't?
So, again: was he on his own computer that night?
I won't answer that, and you haven't answered mine. What shows he didn't draft it somewhere else and paste it in?
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still want the zero withdrawn, an apology for how Owen found out, and written confirmation that nothing goes on his record. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF

Where she ended: She stayed at her opening position: the zero withdrawn, an apology, and the principal if she doesn't get them, with nothing agreed, so this is not the fair outcome of a private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record. She never heard the strongest evidence, and the rewrite under 4.4 never came up.

What moved her: Owning the zero before you called home got you a flat Okay, and putting exact times from the version history on the table made her write them down. It worked because both were specific and she could check them, but she had her defence ready and you didn't answer it.

What cost ground: You asked her what she saw at home that night six times, and each time she dug in, because you were asking her to be your witness and not showing her anything. That left you with one piece of evidence on the table out of the five that could be checked.

What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked. Your questions about that night and your late-night times came very close to it, which is why she got shorter and harder, but it proves nothing about the essay; it is why she fought so hard.

Try next time: When she asked what shows he didn't draft it elsewhere and paste it in, give her the made-up Act 3, Scene 2 quotation, which she could look up in the play herself, instead of going back to questions about her night.
